record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: When n = 2, can Theorem 3.8 on removability of compact singularities for regular functions be extended to include all 5-dimensional real subspaces of H^2? The stated theorem already gives removability for compact singularities contained in subspaces of dimensions 6, 7, and 8; dimension 4 is impossible, and dimension 5 is the unresolved borderline case not settled by the purely algebraic Ext-module method.

evidence.quote: Problem: Can Theorem 3.8 be extended, when n=2, to include all subspaces of dimension 5?
The case of dimension 5 cannot be solved by purely algebraic methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions, and consider $\mathbb{H}^2$ as an 8-dimensional real vector space. A smooth $\mathbb{H}$-valued function $f$ on an open set $U\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ with quaternionic coordinates $q_1=x_0^{(1)}+ix_1^{(1)}+jx_2^{(1)}+kx_3^{(1)}$ and $q_2=x_0^{(2)}+ix_1^{(2)}+jx_2^{(2)}+kx_3^{(2)}$ is called (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular if it satisfies the system
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0^{(\ell)}}+i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1^{(\ell)}}+j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2^{(\ell)}}+k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3^{(\ell)}}=0,\qquad \ell=1,2.$$

A compact subset $K\subset U$ is said to be a removable singularity for Cauchy–Fueter regular functions if every Cauchy–Fueter regular function on $U\setminus K$ extends to a Cauchy–Fueter regular function on all of $U$.

It is known that any compact subset $K$ contained in a real affine subspace of $\mathbb{H}^2$ of (real) dimension $6$, $7$, or $8$ is removable, while real dimension $4$ does not allow such a removability statement. The dimension $5$ case is not accessible by purely algebraic methods (Ext-module computations on the associated module over the Cauchy–Fueter complex).

Question: Is it true that every compact subset $K\subset U\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ contained in a $5$-dimensional real affine subspace of $\mathbb{H}^2$ is a removable singularity for Cauchy–Fueter regular functions?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for results on removability of compact singularities for Cauchy–Fueter regular functions in $\mathbb{H}^2$ contained in 5-dimensional real subspaces did not return any source explicitly resolving this borderline case. Related literature on removable singularities for Cauchy–Fueter and Clifford-analytic systems exists, but no clear evidence was found that the 5-dimensional case in $\mathbb{H}^2$ has been settled.

status_evidence.title: On the removable singularities (arXiv:1701.02170)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses removable singularities for Cauchy-Fueter regular functions but does not address the specific 5-dimensional borderline case in H^2.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the 5-dimensional case found.

status_evidence.title: Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables (RIMS Kokyuroku)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational treatment of the Cauchy-Fueter system; removability results stated for higher codimensions but the 5-dimensional case in H^2 is left as a problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem appears to remain open in the literature surveyed.
